text: 就人类那点可怜的大脑算力，就不要追求信息爆炸了。
en: With humans' pitiful little brain computing power, don't pursue information explosion.

text: 最实用的方式不是避免信息茧房，而是去到正确的茧房。
en: The most practical way is not to avoid information cocoons, but to go to the right cocoon.

text: 关注我就是一种正确的茧房
en: Following me is a kind of right cocoon.

text: 其实很简单，多问为什么，问得越多，解决得问题越多，就越知道要看什么信息，哪里去找合适的信息。
en: Actually it's very simple: ask 'why' more. The more you ask, the more problems you solve, and the more you know what information to look at and where to find suitable information.

text: 如果不知道从哪里开始，可以找限定词多的部分，越是限定，越是绝对就越有必要问，越是跳过逻辑过程给结果，就越是要问：
en: If you don't know where to start, you can look for parts with many qualifiers. The more qualified, the more absolute, the more necessary it is to ask. The more it skips the logical process and gives results, the more you should ask:

text: 只有…
en: Only…

text: 才…
en: …only then…

text: 没有…
en: Without…

text: 就没有…
en: …there is no…

text: 唯一的。
en: The only one.

text: 也可以挑选生活中习以为常的习俗、看似不可动摇的叙事：
en: You can also pick customs you take for granted in life, and seemingly unshakable narratives:

text: 为什么父母一定要求我要结婚、为什么不能有gap year、35岁明明离退休那么远为什么公司都不要、社会时钟为什么会自发的形成并遵守，离开社会时钟的代价是什么。
en: Why must parents demand that I get married? Why can't there be a gap year? At 35, retirement is clearly so far away, why don't companies want us? Why does the social clock form spontaneously and get obeyed, and what is the cost of leaving the social clock?

text: 或者去挑战叙事中的逻辑漏洞：
en: Or challenge logical loopholes in narratives:

text: 百善孝为先，那么如果我爸要和我单挑，「站在原地被打死」和「还击把他摁在地上」哪个比较孝顺。
en: Filial piety is the foremost of all virtues — so if my dad wants to fight me one-on-one, which is more filial: 'standing still and being beaten to death' or 'fighting back and pinning him to the ground'?

text: 中医医生如何通过望闻问切的手段来最终得出「心脏起搏器需要换电池」的结论，并可以让患者在药房抓到规格合适的电池。
en: How does a TCM doctor, through observation, listening/smelling, questioning and pulse-taking, finally reach the conclusion that 'the pacemaker needs a battery change', and allow the patient to pick up a suitably sized battery at the pharmacy?

text: 不同的路由器和天线的摆放位置对家居风水有影响，那么不同的频段、信道、频宽和天线的MMIO分组分别对风水有什么直接影响。
en: If the placement of different routers and antennas affects home feng shui, then what direct effects do different frequency bands, channels, bandwidths and antenna MMIO groupings have on feng shui?

text: 如果这些问题你不能依靠搜索思考翻书解决，找个ai。
en: If you cannot solve these questions by searching, thinking or flipping through books, find an AI.

text: 如果你找到的ai也不能解决，换个ai。
en: If the AI you find cannot solve them either, switch to another AI.

text: 如果你不知道怎么换个能解决问题的ai
en: If you don't know how to switch to an AI that can solve problems,

text: 请打开抖音，开大音量，lets party 🎉！
en: Please open Douyin, turn up the volume, lets party 🎉!

text: 从小教育孩子，学好外语，哪怕被恐怖分子抓了，能喊一声大爷饶命，活着的机会就能大很多。
en: Educate children from a young age to learn foreign languages well. Even if caught by terrorists, being able to shout 'Grandpa, spare my life' greatly increases the chance of staying alive.

text: 一个只会比划的人质和一个能聊天的人质。
en: A hostage who can only gesture versus a hostage who can chat.

text: 会说话的人总比哑巴的生存机会大。
en: Someone who can speak always has a greater chance of survival than a mute.

text: 瞎子和聋子。
en: The blind and the deaf.

text: 朋友给我讲了一个小故事:
en: A friend told me a little story:

text: 一个聋子带着一个瞎子走路。
en: A deaf man walks with a blind man.

text: 聋子说前面有条蛇，瞎子说，怪不得我刚刚听到浠浠索索的声音。
en: The deaf man says there is a snake ahead; the blind man says, no wonder I just heard rustling sounds.

text: 走近了聋子又说是条死蛇。
en: Walking closer, the deaf man says it is a dead snake.

text: 瞎子说怪不得我闻到了臭味。
en: The blind man says, no wonder I smelled a stink.

text: 画面感很强了。
en: The imagery is very strong.

text: 喜剧，极荒诞啊！
en: Comedy, extremely absurd!

text: 聋子知道瞎子看不见。
en: The deaf man knows the blind man cannot see.

text: 瞎子说啥聋子又听不到。
en: Whatever the blind man says, the deaf man cannot hear.

text: 聋子听不到声音，但能看见蛇并判断其生死；瞎子看不见东西，但能听到声音、闻到臭味。
en: The deaf man cannot hear sounds, but can see the snake and judge whether it is alive or dead; the blind man cannot see things, but can hear sounds and smell stinks.

text: 两人的行为准确无误打在对方缺陷上，而又毫不违和。
en: Their behaviours accurately hit each other's defects, yet without any incongruity.

text: 两个人的感官错位造成了信息不对称。
en: The two people's sensory misalignment creates information asymmetry.

text: 这是生理上的。
en: This is physiological.

text: 聋子缺失听觉信息、瞎子缺失视觉信息，本质上是因为双方的感官缺陷，无法获取对方拥有的关键信息，造成完全的信息不对称。
en: The deaf man lacks auditory information, the blind man lacks visual information. Essentially, because of both parties' sensory defects, they cannot obtain key information the other possesses, causing complete information asymmetry.

text: 这样一分析就发现这故事太贴近生活了。
en: Analysing it this way, you find this story is too close to life.

text: 现实中聋子和瞎子好像不少。
en: In reality, there seem to be quite a few deaf and blind people.

text: 一是互动者都在线又都不在线。
en: First: interactors are both online and offline.

text: 都针对对方不具备的功能展示自己。
en: Both display themselves targeting functions the other does not possess.

text: 信息无法真正到达对方，隔离严重。
en: Information cannot truly reach the other party; isolation is severe.

text: 为了刷存在感，鸡同鸭讲。
en: To brush up presence, chickens talk to ducks.

text: 虚假合作，对他人的悲欢不能感同身受。
en: False cooperation, unable to empathise with others' joys and sorrows.

text: 表面一团和气，其实各自为政。
en: Seemingly harmonious on the surface, but actually each doing their own thing.

text: 有点像很多夫妻关系，上下级关系。
en: A bit like many husband-wife relationships, superior-subordinate relationships.

text: 二是反过来理解，为了证明自己有能力，不懂装懂，甚至编造故事来制造效果，结果反而漏洞百出，成了一个笑话。
en: Second, understood in reverse: to prove oneself capable, pretending to understand when one doesn't, even fabricating stories to create effects, resulting in being full of loopholes and becoming a joke.

text: 三是附和顺应。
en: Third: echoing and conforming.

text: 这个故事里瞎子是从属者，但是瞎子为了自保，违心附和，但却忽略了关键信息，踩在了对方的无知和知识空白上。
en: In this story, the blind man is the subordinate, but to protect himself, the blind man insincerely echoes, yet ignores key information, stepping on the other party's ignorance and knowledge gaps.

text: 后果很严重。
en: The consequences are serious.

text: 同一件事，信息来源、信息传递和信息接收会带来信息偏差，甚至信息隔离。
en: For the same matter, information sources, information transmission and information reception bring information bias, even information isolation.

text: 有人刷抖音只看推送的，有人只看头条，有人只看工具书…
en: Some people scroll Douyin and only watch pushes, some only watch headlines, some only read reference books…

text: 不论主动的还是被动的，对信息的筛选方式和吸收不同，认知结果也不同，对事件得出的结论也完全不同。
en: Whether active or passive, different ways of filtering and absorbing information lead to different cognitive results, and completely different conclusions about events.

text: 一句话，信息差带来认知差。
en: In one sentence: information gaps bring cognitive gaps.

text: 回到了一个热词:信息茧房
en: Back to a hot term: information cocoon.

text: 是的，信息茧房会直接导致信息隔离。
en: Yes, information cocoons directly cause information isolation.

text: 信息爆炸的科学时代，看似信息满天飞，思想多元化，但是信息偏差和信息隔离可能堪比没有电灯电泡之前。
en: In the scientific era of information explosion, seemingly information flies everywhere and thoughts are diversified, but information bias and information isolation may rival the time before electric lights and bulbs.

text: 因为蚕茧的包裹，加上精神的懒惰，得到的都是自己喜欢的，大数据天天推给男人:女人是地男人是天，女人要持家主内，不要抛头露脸去做事。
en: Because of the cocoon's wrapping, plus mental laziness, what you get is all what you like. Big data pushes to men every day: women are earth, men are heaven; women should manage the household and stay inside, not show their faces in public to work.

text: 做好家务是本分，伺候好老公是本能…
en: Doing housework well is one's duty; serving one's husband well is instinct…

text: 他如果本身认知能力就孱弱，可怜的大脑经不起这样攻击啊。
en: If his own cognitive ability is weak, his pitiful brain cannot withstand such attacks.

text: 如果无法触及茧房之外的信息，最终认知会困在一个固定的圈圈里，形成偏见，与真正的信息事实上的脱节。
en: If unable to access information outside the cocoon, cognition will eventually be trapped in a fixed circle, forming prejudices, disconnected from true information and facts.

text: 被收割，被奴役，被剥削，被抛弃…
en: Being harvested, enslaved, exploited, abandoned…

text: 唉，说的就是我——和我们。
en: Alas, that's me — and us.

text: 话说我发出的这些信息也许很平庸，一定有我的认知偏差。
en: That said, the information I send out may be mediocre; there must be my cognitive biases.

text: 以上仅供参考，支持点赞飘过～～
en: For reference only. Support, like, and drift by~~

text: 我发现信息茧房最可怕的地方，不是“你看不到别的观点”。
en: I find the most terrifying aspect of information cocoons is not 'you cannot see other views'.

text: 而是你会慢慢产生一种错觉：
en: But that you slowly develop an illusion:

text: “大家都是这么想的。
en: 'Everyone thinks this way.'

text: 你刷短视频，连续看到十条都在说某个行业不行。
en: You scroll short videos and see ten in a row saying a certain industry is failing.

text: 你打开评论区，前几十条也都在附和。
en: You open the comments section, and the first dozens are also echoing.

text: 于是你很容易觉得：
en: So you easily feel:

text: “看来这就是事实。
en: 'It seems this is the fact.'

text: 可你忘了一个问题：
en: But you forget a question:

text: 平台不是在给你展示世界，而是在给你展示你最容易继续看的世界。
en: Platforms are not showing you the world; they are showing you the world you are most likely to keep watching.

text: 所以想避免活在信息茧房里，我觉得最重要的，不是“少上网”，而是别只顺着算法喂给你的东西走。
en: So to avoid living in information cocoons, I think the most important thing is not 'going online less', but not only following what algorithms feed you.

text: 第一，看到特别符合自己观点的内容，反而要多留个心眼
en: First: when you see content particularly consistent with your own views, be extra careful.

text: 这个特别重要。
en: This is particularly important.

text: 因为人最容易相信的，往往不是最真的信息。
en: Because what people most easily believe is often not the truest information.

text: 而是最符合自己原本想法的信息。
en: But the information most consistent with their original ideas.

text: 比如你本来就觉得某个职业没前途。
en: For example, you already think a certain profession has no future.

text: 刷到一条“劝退帖”，你会马上点进去。
en: Scrolling to a 'dissuasion post', you immediately click in.

text: 再来一条，又点。
en: Another one comes, and you click again.

text: 平台一看：
en: The platform sees:

text: 哦，你爱看这个。
en: Oh, you love watching this.

text: 接下来全给你推“这个行业完了”。
en: Next, it pushes you all 'this industry is finished'.

text: 过几天你会产生一种错觉：
en: After a few days, you develop an illusion:

text: “网上所有人都这么说。
en: 'Everyone online says this.'

text: 其实不是。
en: Actually not.

text: 只是算法越来越懂你。
en: It's just that algorithms understand you better and better.

text: 所以我现在看到特别顺耳的观点，会故意问一句：
en: So now when I see particularly pleasing views, I deliberately ask:

text: “有没有跟这个结论相反的证据？
en: 'Is there evidence contrary to this conclusion?'

text: 这句话特别有用。
en: This sentence is particularly useful.

text: 第二，主动搜“反面词”
en: Second: proactively search for 'opposite terms'.

text: 这个方法特别简单。
en: This method is particularly simple.

text: 比如你准备买一款产品。
en: For example, you are preparing to buy a product.

text: 别只搜：
en: Don't only search:

text: “XX值不值得买？
en: 'Is XX worth buying?'

text: 再搜：
en: Then search:

text: “XX缺点”
en: 'XX shortcomings'

text: “XX退货”
en: 'XX returns'

text: “XX后悔”
en: 'XX regrets'

text: 想进入一个行业也是。
en: Wanting to enter an industry is the same.

text: 别只搜：
en: Don't only search:

text: “XX行业前景。
en: 'XX industry prospects.'

text: 再搜：
en: Then search:

text: “XX行业离职”
en: 'XX industry resignations'

text: “XX行业劝退”
en: 'XX industry dissuasion'

text: “XX行业真实收入”
en: 'XX industry real income'

text: 不是为了把所有事情都想坏。
en: Not to think everything badly.

text: 而是为了让自己至少看到另一面。
en: But to at least see the other side.

text: 算法喜欢把你往一个方向推，你得主动往反方向走两步。
en: Algorithms like to push you in one direction; you must proactively walk two steps in the opposite direction.

text: 第三，少看“别人总结后的观点”，多找原始信息
en: Third: watch less 'views summarised by others', find more original information.

text: 这个我现在越来越在意。
en: I care about this more and more now.

text: 一个政策出来，短视频已经开始：
en: When a policy comes out, short videos have already started:

text: “重大变化！
en: 'Major changes!'

text: “普通人一定要注意！
en: 'Ordinary people must pay attention!'

text: 可真正点开原文，可能发现根本不是他说的那个意思。
en: But actually clicking the original text, you may find it is not at all what he said.

text: 一项研究出来，网上标题写：
en: When a study comes out, online headlines write:

text: “研究证明某某一定怎样。
en: 'Research proves XX must be so.'

text: 可原研究可能只是说：
en: But the original study may only say:

text: “存在一定关联。
en: 'There is a certain association.'

text: 信息经过一层层转述以后，会越来越刺激，越来越绝对。
en: After information passes through layers of retelling, it becomes more and more stimulating, more and more absolute.

text: 所以涉及重要决定时，尽量往上找：
en: So for important decisions, try to trace upwards:

text: 政策原文。
en: Policy original text.

text: 完整采访。
en: Complete interviews.

text: 原始数据。
en: Original data.

text: 研究摘要。
en: Research abstracts.

text: 财报。
en: Financial reports.

text: 法院文书。
en: Court documents.

text: 别永远喝别人嚼过三遍的水。
en: Don't always drink water chewed three times by others.

text: 第四，别只关注“你喜欢的人”
en: Fourth: don't only follow 'people you like'.

text: 很多人关注账号的逻辑是：
en: Many people's logic for following accounts is:

text: 这个人说得真对。
en: This person speaks so rightly.

text: 关注。
en: Follow.

text: 另一个人说得也对。
en: Another person also speaks rightly.

text: 继续关注。
en: Continue following.

text: 最后你的信息流里，全部都是“跟你一样的人”。
en: In the end, your information stream is entirely 'people like you'.

text: 这当然很舒服。
en: This is certainly comfortable.

text: 但也最容易封闭。
en: But also easiest to close off.

text: 所以可以故意保留几类账号：
en: So you can deliberately keep several types of accounts:

text: 跟你观点不一样，但愿意讲证据的人。
en: People with views different from yours, but willing to present evidence.

text: 你不熟悉行业里的专业人士。
en: Professionals in industries unfamiliar to you.

text: 不同年龄、不同职业、不同生活方式的人。
en: People of different ages, professions, and lifestyles.

text: 重点不是关注那些天天骂人的账号。
en: The point is not to follow accounts that curse people every day.

text: 而是关注：
en: But to follow:

text: “我不一定认同他，但他能让我看到另一个角度。
en: 'I may not agree with him, but he lets me see another angle.'

text: 这才有价值。
en: This is valuable.

text: 第五，评论区别只看热评
en: Fifth: don't only read hot comments in comment sections.

text: 这一点特别容易被忽略。
en: This point is particularly easy to overlook.

text: 热评不一定最正确。
en: Hot comments are not necessarily the most correct.

text: 它只是最容易引起共鸣。
en: They are just the easiest to resonate with.

text: 情绪最强、表达最爽的评论，往往更容易被顶上去。
en: Comments with the strongest emotions and most satisfying expression are often pushed to the top.

text: 可真正有信息量的东西，有时候藏在下面：
en: But truly informative things are sometimes hidden below:

text: “我是这个行业的，实际情况是…
en: 'I am in this industry; the actual situation is…'

text: “这里有个数据不太对…
en: 'There is a data point here that is not quite right…'

text: “这个案例只适用于某种情况…
en: 'This case only applies to certain situations…'

text: 所以看评论的时候，别只看前三条。
en: So when reading comments, don't only read the first three.

text: 尤其是争议话题，多翻一翻。
en: Especially for controversial topics, scroll more.

text: 你会发现，同一件事常常比标题复杂得多。
en: You will find that the same matter is often much more complex than the title.

text: 第六，学会区分“事实”和“观点”
en: Sixth: learn to distinguish 'facts' from 'views'.

text: 比如：
en: For example:

text: “某公司今年裁员500人。
en: 'A certain company laid off 500 people this year.'

text: 这是事实。
en: This is a fact.

text: “这个行业彻底没救了。
en: 'This industry is completely hopeless.'

text: 这是判断。
en: This is a judgment.

text: “某城市房价同比下降。
en: 'A certain city's housing prices fell year-on-year.'

text: 这是事实。
en: This is a fact.

text: “现在买房的人都会后悔。
en: 'People buying houses now will all regret it.'

text: 这是观点。
en: This is a view.

text: 我们特别容易把有数据包装的观点，当成事实。
en: We particularly easily mistake views packaged with data for facts.

text: 所以看到一条信息，可以问：
en: So when you see a piece of information, you can ask:

text: “哪一部分是已经发生的，哪一部分只是这个人的解释？
en: 'Which part has already happened, and which part is just this person's interpretation?'

text: 这一分开，脑子马上清楚很多。
en: Once separated, your mind immediately becomes much clearer.

text: 第七，别把“反对主流”误认为独立思考
en: Seventh: don't mistake 'opposing the mainstream' for independent thinking.

text: 这一点也挺重要。
en: This point is also quite important.

text: 有些人意识到信息茧房以后，会走向另一个极端：
en: Some people, after realising information cocoons, go to another extreme:

text: “大家都这么说，那我偏不信。
en: 'Everyone says so, but I refuse to believe it.'

text: 其实这也不叫独立思考。
en: Actually, this is not independent thinking either.

text: 真正的独立思考不是：
en: True independent thinking is not:

text: 别人说东，我偏说西。
en: Others say east, I insist on west.

text: 而是：
en: But:

text: 证据指向哪里，我就暂时相信哪里。
en: Wherever evidence points, I temporarily believe there.

text: 哪怕最后发现“大多数人说得对”，也没关系。
en: Even if finally discovering 'most people are right', it doesn't matter.

text: 独立思考不是为了显得与众不同。
en: Independent thinking is not to appear different.

text: 是为了减少被情绪牵着走。
en: It is to reduce being led by emotions.

text: 第八，定期清理自己的信息流
en: Eighth: regularly clean up your information stream.

text: 这个特别实用。
en: This is particularly practical.

text: 隔一段时间看看自己关注的人：
en: Every so often, look at the people you follow:

text: 是不是全在讲同一种东西？
en: Are they all talking about the same thing?

text: 是不是每天刷到的内容越来越像？
en: Is the content you scroll to every day becoming more and more similar?

text: 是不是看完以后只剩愤怒、焦虑、比较？
en: After watching, are you left only with anger, anxiety, comparison?

text: 如果是，就主动换一批。
en: If so, proactively switch to a new batch.

text: 增加一点长内容。
en: Add a bit of long content.

text: 加几个不同领域。
en: Add a few different fields.

text: 少看纯情绪输出。
en: Watch less pure emotional output.

text: 信息流其实也是一种环境。
en: Information streams are actually a kind of environment.

text: 你每天泡在哪里，脑子慢慢就会变成哪里的样子。
en: Where you soak every day, your brain slowly becomes like that place.

text: 最后
en: Finally,

text: 我现在越来越觉得，避免信息茧房，不是让自己什么都看、什么都信。
en: I increasingly feel that avoiding information cocoons is not about watching everything and believing everything.

text: 那样更乱。
en: That would be even messier.

text: 真正有用的是养成几个习惯：
en: What truly works is developing a few habits:

text: 顺耳的观点，多怀疑一下。
en: For pleasing views, doubt a bit more.

text: 刺耳但有证据的观点，多看两眼。
en: For harsh but evidenced views, look twice more.

text: 重要信息，尽量找源头。
en: For important information, try to find the source.

text: 做决定以前，主动找一次反方。
en: Before making decisions, proactively seek the opposing side once.

text: 因为这个时代真正稀缺的，不是信息。
en: Because in this era, what is truly scarce is not information.

text: 而是一个人看到一堆信息以后，还能保留一句：
en: But that a person, after seeing a pile of information, can still retain one sentence:

text: “等等，这只是我现在看到的部分。
en: 'Wait, this is only the part I see now.'

text: 能保留这句话，就已经很不容易被困住了。
en: Being able to retain this sentence means you are already not easily trapped.
